philosophy.summary: Empty space between star systems impacts the sense of a vast galaxy being traversed
philosophy.quote: Stars are now 10x spread out, starting fuel is 500 to compensate... much more like the feel of traveling through a vast galaxy

philosophy.summary: Authenticity requires understanding original game's design, not just copying superficially
philosophy.quote: The original SC2 hyperspace is NOT a zoomed-out star map. It's a first-person flying view — you're flying through red space and stars pass by you. The star map is a separate screen you bring up from a menu.

philosophy.summary: Different systems use different angle conventions; must understand both to translate between them correctly
philosophy.quote: The sprite frame selection formula has a `+ Math.PI/2` offset that creates a 90-degree mismatch between the visual direction and the actual movement/firing direction.

portrait: This is a session of iterative game refinement focused on authenticity to Star Control 2. Fibonacci is building a browser-based SC2 game and repeatedly asks to make systems look and feel exactly like the original—outfit screens using real UQM assets, star maps with 500+ authentic stars spread across a vast galaxy, hyperspace with glowing sprite-based stars rather than flat squares. The AI systematically researches original game mechanics through UQM source code, implements fixes (sprite rotation, projectile direction, outfit screen layout), and responds to user feedback with increasingly faithful recreations. The session demonstrates deep technical problem-solving: understanding coordinate conventions, researching asset mappings, analyzing source code architectures, and balancing visual authenticity with implementation constraints. By end of session, game has SC2-style hyperspace with real star data, 16-module outfit system using UQM graphics, glowing star sprites, and 30x spread between systems for a vaster feel. Work remains on dialogue text updates and final hyperspace refinements.
